Marcus / Laura / Emma — I reviewed FinServ_DPA_Redline_v2.docx and have inline counsel comments. High-level guidance below; inline redline file to follow if you want a tracked version.

1) Subprocessor notice & objection- FinServCo proposes a 14-day notice + objection window. Our standard practice is 30 days to accommodate procurement and operational review; operationally we publish an up-to-date subprocessor list and provide notice for material changes. Proposed compromise: accept 14 days for subprocessors with routine infrastructure access (e.g., monitoring, hosting) and 30 days for subprocessors that process Customer Data beyond infrastructure (e.g., model tuning, analytics). Also add a 10-day cure period for Redwood to remediate before termination rights kick in.

2) Transfer mechanism- We can accept SCCs plus the EU–US Addendum, but we should preserve the ability to update mechanisms as law evolves (e.g., future adequacy or new frameworks). Proposed language: "Redwood will rely on the SCCs and any reasonably necessary additional addendum (including EU–US Addendum) in accordance with applicable law; parties agree to negotiate in good faith any required updates." Avoid unilateral customer insertion of bespoke transfer language that conflicts with operational controls.

3) Audit & access rights- FinServCo requested broad audit rights. We are amenable to SOC 2 Type II and periodic security attestations; for on-site audits, we prefer a third-party SOC audit review or a scope-limited review with notice and cost allocation.

4) Liability & indemnity- Some of the redlines broaden indemnity and remove caps. We should push back on uncapped liability for regulatory fines but can accept carveouts for gross negligence and will propose a balanced cap tied to fees.

5) E‑sign & execution- DocuSign is fine. Once commercial and counsel agree we can route a single DocuSign envelope for an executed DPA.

Next steps: Marcus / Laura — confirm whether sales are able to accept the proposed 14 vs 30-day split and the liability cap guidance. I'll prepare a tracked redline with the suggested language and propose a DocuSign envelope text for signature.

Neha Kapoor
Privacy Counsel, Redwood Inference
